JUDGEMENT CALLS
  S23 (880,608), C6 x R2, deg4 -> CROSSING, overriding the tracer's junction default. This is the one intersection on the sheet where the drafter drew a plain X (inkmap shows two clean 3px strokes crossing, no blob - dot score 1.4 - and no hop) instead of his usual semicircle, so the ink prior would say 'junction'. Electrical impossibility decides it the other way: as a junction, C6 (which already carries V-DC #10's right lead) would merge with C5 (which carries V-DC #10's left lead), short-circuiting V-DC #10 and also shorting I-DC #8. The three neighbouring sites that could have relieved that short instead - S20 (C5 terminating on R2), S28 (C4 terminating on R3) and S29 (R3 terminating on C6) - are all unambiguous T's in their crops, so S23 is the only place the separation can live. Reading it as a junction would collapse n4 and net 0 into a single 10-terminal node and short two sources.
  Bridge B0 (402,178)->(402,172), the top tip of rail C3 reaching row R0: KEPT. inkmap shows a 4-pixel white gap at x=400 between y=174 and y=177, but the zoom at 12x shows a pen lead-in aimed straight at the row and the drafter attached every other rail (C2 at S4, C4 at S3, C5 at S2) to R0 the same way. Dropping the bridge would split n3 into {I-AC #2 right, V-DC #5 left} and {Inductor #3 right, Capacitor #6 left}, giving 7 nets instead of 6; both readings are electrically sane, so this one rests on the ink and on the drafter's habit.
